scope: Low-level DXF group-5 identity emission for DBCOLOR.

behavior: The writer remaps and reserves a nonzero source identity, or allocates an identity when the source handle is zero.
The source object identity is bound only after staged record output succeeds.
A fixed output identity is refused before publishing record bytes.
Late invalid-XDATA failure restores staged bytes, emitted-record inventory, and source-object identity-map changes; corrected retry is verified with a fresh writer.

validationProfile.source: Locally constructed in-memory AC1032 DBCOLOR records. No DWG/DXF fixtures were added.
cases: Mapped group-5 identity, OBJECTS inventory identity, and source-object binding.
Typed callback readback checks true-color and color-book names.
Allocated group-5 identity when the source handle is zero, with typed readback.
Fixed-handle remap refusal preserves the destination.
Late invalid-XDATA rollback checks destination bytes, emitted-record inventory, and source-object identity map.
Corrected retry and typed readback use a fresh writer.
Existing standard object-identity, unsupported CMC-method, and retained color-book budget controls still pass.

limitations: Generated identity and field transport only; physical DBCOLOR producer prevalence and complete-document support are not established.
Native color-book acceptance and consumer color appearance remain open.
The late-failure test verifies byte, inventory, and source-object identity-map rollback, not handle-allocator reservation rollback; retry is verified on a fresh writer.
next: Continue checking remaining low-level OBJECTS identity routes; keep physical producer and native color semantics gated on independent evidence.
